summary: Mobile OCR timezone normalization bug causing duplicate per-diem reimbursements
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (internal Redwood employees) submitting per-diem claims via the Redwood mobile app are intermittently creating duplicate reimbursement entries in the expense ledger. Investigation shows the mobile OCR pipeline normalizes receipt timestamps to UTC incorrectly when the device timezone differs from the account profile timezone, producing slightly different receipt hashes and causing the deduplication step to fail.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate per-diem payments recorded in finance ledger for same day expenses.
- Approximate exposure: small-dollar but frequent (est. $800–1,500/month) and creates reconciliation noise.
- Affects payroll/accounting reconciliation and automated fraud flags for duplicated receipts.

Observed behavior:
- Two claims submitted by same user on same calendar date with identical images are persisted as unique receipts in ledger.
- OCR metadata shows different "captured_at" values when device timezone is non-UTC and app is offline then syncs.

Expected behavior:
- Receipt hashing and dedupe should ignore timezone-only offsets so identical images map to the same canonical receipt ID regardless of capture timezone or delayed sync.

Notes: preliminary triage points to a timezone-normalization step added to OCR metadata in mobile-sdk v2.4.0 that coerces captured_at to UTC but uses local-device offset inconsistently when sync occurs after midnight in user-local time.
steps_to_reproduce: On device with timezone set to America/Los_Angeles, create an account profile with timezone Europe/London.
Open mobile app v2.4.0, photograph a standard per-diem receipt just before local midnight (e.g., 23:58 PDT).
Disable network (airplane mode), wait until after midnight local device time, then re-enable network so app syncs.
Observe two receipt records in the expense UI and two ledger entries after automated sync (one with capture timestamp shifted).

comments: Support (Maya): Initial report received from payroll with three user complaints about duplicate per-diem lines in Feb payroll run. Attached sample receipt images and claim IDs.
Finance (Ishaan Patel): Noted duplicate rows in March AP export - will hold payments for flagged users until dedupe rule fixed. Requesting immediate mitigation steps.

Mobile Eng (Oliver Grant): Reproduced locally using steps above. Suspect mobile-sdk timezone coercion + offline sync ordering. Creating PR to adjust normalization logic and to include original image hash in dedupe key.

SRE (Lena Ortiz): Observed increased error rate in dedupe metrics dashboard after v2.4.0 rollout to ~40% of active mobile users. Rolling back not feasible; recommending server-side patch to dedupe service as temporary mitigation.
Support (Maya): Marking as P1 due to impact on payroll reconciliation and Finance hold. SLA first response met. Will coordinate communication with payroll and affected employees.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: reimbursements-engine dedupe key updated server-side to include normalized_image_hash and original_device_hash; Finance set automated rule to collapse receipts with matching image hashes and same user/date for March payroll export. Mobile SDK patch PR merged to fix timezone coercion (mobile-sdk PR #1847).
follow_up_actions: Deploy reimbursements-engine hotfix to prod-us-east (target 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC).
Release mobile-sdk v2.4.1 to address timezone coercion and add explicit device-timestamp metadata (QA required).
Finance to run a one-off dedupe job for Feb–Mar exports and reconcile impacted payouts (owner: Ishaan Patel).
Add monitoring alert for dedupe-failure-rate > 0.5% and a runbook for payroll holds (owner: SRE).
financial_impact_estimate: Estimated duplicate payouts: $800–1,500/month. Projected one-time reconciliation effort ~4–8 engineer-hours + 2 finance hours.
